column1: # FIX-928 — duplicate ACTIVE entity_grants on prod. MANIFEST ONLY: nothing applied 2026-09-06.
# READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING ANYTHING.
# FIX-928's premise was "add a partial unique index on active grants". That index
# ALREADY EXISTS and has since before this audit:
#   entity_grants_unique_active
#     UNIQUE (user_id, role, target_type, target_id) WHERE status = 'active'
# It is not missing. It is UNREACHABLE for global-scoped grants, because
# target_type='global' carries target_id IS NULL and a B-tree unique index treats
# every NULL as distinct. So the constraint holds perfectly for jurisdiction- and
# official-scoped grants and does nothing at all for global ones. Adding the index
# FIX-928 describes would be a no-op.
# Prod census 2026-09-06, active grants grouped by (user_id, role, target_type, target_id):
#   exactly ONE violating group — 13 rows, all NULL target_id.
# The other group the coarser (user_id, role, target_type) query surfaces —
# abd54530.../constituent/jurisdiction, 5 rows — is NOT a duplicate set: those are
# five different jurisdictions and the index is doing its job on them. Do not
# retire any of those five.
# SHAPE OF THE 13: one row at 2026-06-19 09:41:39, then SIX PAIRS ~200-250 ms apart
# and all have expires_at NULL. A ~200 ms pair is a double-submit, not a human
# granting twice; the write path has no idempotency and the six pairs are six
# double-fires. That is a second defect and it is NOT fixed by any dedupe.
# WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A TIDINESS PROBLEM — the revoke path is single-row:
#   apps/civitics/app/api/admin/grants/[id]/route.ts:118-121
#     await admin.from("entity_grants").update({ status: "revoked" }).eq("id", grantId);
# It revokes ONE row by primary key. Revoking this user's staff/global access
# through the admin UI therefore flips 1 of 13 rows, returns {ok:true,
# status:"revoked"}, and leaves 12 ACTIVE. Every has-grant check is an EXISTS over
# status='active', so the user keeps full platform-staff access while the admin who
# revoked it has been told, truthfully as far as the route knows, that it is gone.
# A revocation UI that reports success and does not revoke is a security finding,
# not a data-hygiene one. FIX-928's severity should be raised accordingly.
# NOT the same 13 as the "13" in packages/data/src/pipelines/integrity-audit/checks/
# grants.ts:124 — that line counts anon/authenticated-EXECUTEable PROCEDUREs that
# FIX-1113 revoked. Unrelated coincidence of number. Do not conflate them.
# DISPOSITION: keep the OLDEST row per key, retire the rest. Retire = set
# status='revoked' (the enum's existing terminal value), never DELETE — grant_events
# and grant_evidence reference these rows and the history is the audit trail.
# NOT APPLIED TODAY. The dedupe plus the durable constraint are a Craig-gated set:
#   1. retire the 12 RETIRE rows below
#   2. close the NULL hole — a second partial unique index
#        UNIQUE (user_id, role, target_type) WHERE status='active' AND target_id IS NULL
#      alongside the existing one, so both the NULL and non-NULL cases are covered
#   3. make the revoke path revoke the KEY, not the row id
#   4. make the grant path idempotent so a double-submit cannot mint a second row
# Steps 3 and 4 matter more than 1 and 2: dedupe without them just resets the clock.
